sections.h2: What does the Beaver County Recorder of Deeds do?
sections.html:
The office files the deeds, mortgages and related papers that make a property sale part of the public record in Beaver County. It sits in the Third Street section on the first floor of the Beaver County Courthouse at 810 Third Street in Beaver, and the phone is 724-770-4560. Counter hours run 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday.

Recording in Beaver County started in 1800, the year the county was created, and every record has since been digitized. Besides deeds and mortgages, the office takes sheriff deeds, tax claim deeds, satisfactions, assignments, releases, restrictive covenants, leases, installment land contracts, Clean and Green filings and notary bonds. It also collects the Pennsylvania realty transfer tax and passes the local share to the municipality and school district.

If you own a house here, the office offers a free Fraud Alert sign-up that sends a notice whenever a deed or mortgage is recorded under your name. Others in the county may share your name, so check any alert against your own property before reacting.

sections.h2: Where is Beaver County, and who sells a house there?
sections.html:
Beaver County sits in the Greater Pittsburgh region, was formed on March 12, 1800 from parts of Allegheny and Washington counties, and takes its name from the Beaver River. It covers 444 square miles, about 9 of them water. The Ohio River cuts through the county and separates the southern third from the northern two thirds, and Beaver is the county seat while Aliquippa is the largest city. Beaver Falls is the county's other city, and the rest of the map is boroughs and townships.

Census QuickFacts puts the 2025 population estimate at 166,032, a drop of 1.3% from the 2020 base. The county counts 79,845 housing units and 72,257 households, and 75.0% of homes are owner-occupied. For owner-occupied homes the median value in 2020 to 2024 was $190,900, and median gross rent was $890. Residents 65 and older make up 24.8% of the population, which is why many sales here follow an estate or a move to smaller housing.

Getting around is easy for a buyer who commutes. The Pennsylvania Turnpike, I-376 and US 30 all cross the county, along with a long list of state routes. Climate is the hot-summer humid continental type, with January averages near 29 degrees and July near 73 in the Beaver and Rochester area.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax is due on a Beaver County sale?
sections.html:
The total is 2% of the value being conveyed: 1% to the state and 1% to local governments, split evenly between the municipality and the school district. The county notes that this value is not always the sales price. The Recorder collects all of it at the time of recording and will not accept a deed until the tax is paid.

The state and local governments do not care who pays, so the purchase agreement decides. On most agreements the buyer and seller split it, but the new owner answers for any shortfall if the amount is later questioned. Recording fees and both taxes can go on one check made payable to the Recorder of Deeds, and the office takes only cash or check.

Beaver County transfer tax parts and copy charges, per the Recorder's Taxes and FAQ pages
ItemAmount
State realty transfer tax1% of value
Municipal share0.5% of value
School district share0.5% of value
Copy made at the counter$1.00 per page
Copy by mail$5 flat plus $1.00 per page
Certification of a copy$1.50

The recording fee for a deed changed on December 1, 2025, when a new fee schedule took effect that includes a $1 Criminal Justice Enhancement Account charge under Act 45 of 2025. Ask the Recorder's office for the current schedule before you budget for closing.

sections.h2: What is a statement of value, and what is the common level ratio?
sections.html:
A statement of value is a state form, filed in duplicate, that either sets the value of the property or states the reason a transfer is exempt. The office requires one whenever the tax is not paid or the deed does not show the true value, such as a deed reciting $1.00 of consideration. State investigators can review those filings later.

Completing the form needs the common level ratio for Beaver County. The State Tax Equalization Board set the factor at 1.34, and it applies to documents accepted from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. Under 61 Pa. Code 91.02, the date of acceptance is presumed to be the date of execution written in the deed.

  • Exempt transfers named by the county include those between spouses, parent and child, grandparent and grandchild, siblings, and a stepparent and stepchild.
  • Other exemptions exist for particular situations, and the county points owners to an attorney or the Pennsylvania Department of Revenue.
  • If the state later decides the value was higher, or an exemption does not hold, the Department of Revenue mails a determination. You pay the added state and local tax plus interest to the state, and the Recorder then disburses the local share.

sections.h2: How do you record a deed in Beaver County?
sections.html:
You can bring it to the courthouse or send it by mail. In person, the office says review, receipt and scanning usually take 10 to 15 minutes, and the recorded original is mailed back within about a week. If a mailed package has not arrived after two weeks, the county suggests contacting the Postal Service.

Mailed packages need a check payable to the Recorder of Deeds for the right amount and a self-addressed stamped envelope with enough postage. The office takes no responsibility for postage that falls short or for returns lost by the Postal Service, and the FAQ advises against mailing cash. Most sellers never handle this step, because the title company or closing attorney files the deed. Ask whoever is running your closing to confirm the filing date and send you the recorded copy.

  • Documents that touch more than one municipality need the local tax split clearly stated.
  • Subdivision plans must be 18 by 24 inches or 24 by 36 inches, original on linen or mylar, and cannot be older than 90 days from governing body approval.
  • A veteran's discharge can be recorded through the Veterans Office in the courthouse basement, and the Recorder issues certified copies at no charge.

sections.h2: How do you look up a deed or a mortgage in Beaver County?
sections.html:
Beaver County indexes by name, not by street address or tax parcel number. To find a deed or mortgage you need the name of the grantor, grantee, mortgagor or mortgagee and the approximate year. Parcel numbers come from the Assessment Office, so a seller who only has an address should start there.

Every document in the office is public except military discharge papers, which are impounded. Staff can answer general questions by phone but are not permitted to run searches or give legal advice, so a title searcher or attorney handles anything deeper. To trace ownership backward, read the recital that follows the legal description, usually beginning with the word Being, and follow it through each prior deed toward 1800.

The county records deeds for land only, not buildings. Older deeds sometimes mention when a structure was built, and the price of a conveyance can hint at it, but the Recorder does not keep construction records. Check with the municipality for those.

sections.h2: What should a Beaver County seller do about liens and mortgage satisfactions?
sections.html:
Confirm that the payoff of your existing mortgage ends with a recorded satisfaction piece. The lender starts that step, and it may send you the forms. If it fails to file, you can bring or mail the original satisfaction piece to the Recorder with the fee on the current schedule and a stamped return envelope.

Before you list, pull your own name from the index and read what is recorded against it. Open mortgages, old easements and agreements show up there, and clearing a missing satisfaction is quicker before an offer than during the closing window.

  • Gather the last recorded deed and its recital.
  • Ask the Assessment Office for the parcel number.
  • Ask your lender for the recorded satisfaction on any paid-off loan.
  • Agree in writing who pays the 2% transfer tax.

faqs.q: Who pays the realty transfer tax when a house sells in Beaver County?
faqs.a: The contract decides, and the county's offices do not mind which side pays as long as the full amount is collected at recording. On most agreements the buyer and seller split it, but the new owner is responsible if the amount is questioned later.

faqs.q: What hours is the Beaver County Recorder of Deeds open?
faqs.a: The office is open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, at 810 Third Street in Beaver. The phone number is 724-770-4560, and it is on the first floor of the courthouse in the Third Street section.

faqs.q: Can I pay the recording fee and transfer tax with one check?
faqs.a: Yes. Recording fees plus the state and local taxes can all be on one check made payable to the Recorder of Deeds. The office accepts only cash or check, and it asks you not to mail cash.

faqs.q: Does the Recorder search by address in Beaver County?
faqs.a: No. The indexes are by the names of grantor, grantee, mortgagor and mortgagee, grouped by year. Parcel numbers and addresses are handled by the Assessment Office.

faqs.q: How long does Beaver County take to return a recorded deed?
faqs.a: A walk-in filing is reviewed, receipted and scanned in about 10 to 15 minutes, and the recorded original is mailed back within about a week. If a mailed filing has not come back after two weeks, contact the Postal Service.
